RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the November 28, 2006/Agrahayana 7, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
Promotion of tourism in Assam
†*81. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of
TOURISM be pleased to state:
(a) the details of schemes formulated
by Government for development and
promotion of tourism in Assam; and
(b) the details of amount allocated,
released and spent by the Central
Government for implementation of
proposals regarding tourism in the State
during  the last three years, project-wise?
Upgradation of Biju Patnaik Airport,
Bhubaneswar
*82. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to upgrade
Biju Patnaik Airport (Bhubaneswar) in
Orissa to the international standards;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the time-frame within which the
above project would be initiated and
completed; and
(d) whether during this upgradation scheme
a sizable number of temporary workers
working now shall be made permanent?
Development of Arka Khetra of Konark
*83. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
develop Arka Khetra of Konark to make it
more attractive for the tourists;
(b) whether this project would be
funded by the IOC;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) what is the status of development of
eco-tourism with central assistance in Orissa?
Loans to farmers at concessional
interest rates
†*84. SHRI MOTI LAL VORA:
SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) when Government made an
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

27
announcement to provide loans to farmers
at concessional interest rate;
(b) the States where concessional loans
have been provided to the farmers so far
and the percentage of Co-operative Banks
therein;
(c) the arrangements made by
Government to ensure that the farmers do
not take loan from moneylenders;
(d) the arrangements made by
Government to provide loans immediately
to the farmers in the rest of the States also;
and
(e) the hurdles in providing loans to
farmers through Co-operative Banks and
by when, these would be removed?
Shortage of Commercial pilots
†*85. SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn towards the shortage of
commercial pilots in the country; and
(b) if so, the details of steps taken to
meet the shortage of commercial pilots in
the country?
Losses suffered by domestic airlines
*86. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that almost all
the domestic airlines are incurring low
profits and even in some cases losses as
compared to the previous year;
(b) if so, the details thereof; airline-
wise;
(c) what are the reasons for this; and
(d) the details of steps taken by
Government in this regard?
Training of pilots on CAT-III system
*87. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government  have reviewed
the preparedness of different airlines to
deploy the required number of pilots
trained to navigate jets to thick foggy
conditions, during the fast approaching
winter season, with the help of CAT-III
Instrument Landing System (ILS);
(b) if so, the results thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that several airlines
fall significantly short of the required
number of pilots as per the laid down
norms;
(d)  if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the steps taken to persuade the
concerned airlines to employ more trained
pilots or reschedule their flights during the
poor visibility conditions period ahead to
avoid inconvenience to passengers?
Protection of ASI monuments and
museums
*88. SHRI SANJAY RAUT:
SHRI AJAY MAROO:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ajanta,
which is among the first examples of early
Buddhists architecture  pertaining to 2nd
century BC, is now facing problem of seepage;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

28
(b) if so, what is the number of caves
which are under threat of water seepage;
(c) the details of  the steps taken or
proposed to be taken by Government to
protect this world heritage site;
(d) whether there is  requirement of
more security personnels for curbing the
illegal trafficking and the protection  of
various ASI's monuments and museums in
the country; and
(e) if so, what is Government's response
thereto?
Tourists safety from riots and bomb blasts

SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
drastic fall in the n

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the November 28, 2006/Agrahayana 7, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy Industries
and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas; Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 155
Commencement of flights by German
Airlines between Goa and Germany
554. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN
NAIK: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether German Airlines Condor has
commenced commercial flights between
Goa and Germany;
(b) if so, the frequency of these flights;
(c) whether these flights will be
restricted to the tourist season;
(d) the details of the conditions of
license under which the airlines will be
operating; and
(e) whether any other foreign airlines
have sought permission to operate to and
from Goa?
Reduction in ATF cost
555. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Aviation Turbine Fuel
(ATF) costs are 70 per cent higher in India
which work out to almost 40 per cent of
the total cost input of Indian carriers;
(b) whether Iindian airports will soon
have ATF outlets operated by global ATF
suppliers and if so, to what extent this will
help in reducing the ATF costs for Indian
carriers; and
(c) whether Bangalore, Hyderabad,
Delhi and Mumbai airports are considering
the open access model for the supply of
ATF and if so, how soon these facilities are
likely to be in place?
Casual labours in Indian Airlines
556. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of casual labours working
in Indian Airlines on 90 days basis at
various regions of Mumbai, Kolkata,
Chennai and Delhi (region-wise break up)
and for how long they have been working;
(b) whether these casual labours have
been empanelled for regular vacancies to be
filled up as per the Recruitment and
Promotion Rules of Indian Airlines; and

131
(c) whether the vacancies will be filled
up by the Indian Airlines before the
proposed merger of Air India and Indian
Airlines is completed?
Leasing of aircrafts
557. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) what is the fleet strength of Indian
Airlines and Air India as on 31st October,
2006 (type-wise, owned and leased break
up);
(b) the number of aircrafts which have
been flying out of the leased and owned
aircrafts and how many are grounded as on
31st October, 2006;
(c) the payment conditions for leased
aircrafts when these aircrafts are grounded;
(d) whether lease amount is payable
even if the aircraft is grounded; and
(e) if so, the terms and conditions of the
payment?
Open sky policy
558. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Directorate General of Civil
Aviation has moved a proposal to follow
an open sky policy for four months
beginning from November, 2006;
(b) if so, whether during the open sky
policy, international airlines are allowed to
increase frequency or bring in larger aircraft
irrespective of capacity that they are
allowed under the existing air services
bilateral agreement;
(c) if so, whether Government are keen
to ensure passengers do not feel
inconvenience and seats are easily available
during the upcoming winter season; and
(d) if so, by when a final decision in this
regard is likely to be taken?
Merger of Air India and Indian
Airlines
559. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI VEDPRAKASH P.
GOYAL:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are planning to merge Air India and Indian
Airlines;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the details of benefits of this merger
for Government and all employees?
Theft at airports
†560. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether certain incidents of thefts
in the flights between Delhi-Mumbai,
Delhi-Kolkata and Mumbai-Kolkata have
come to notice;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the extent of loss incurred by each
passenger as a result of such thefts and the
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

132
compensation given by the airline to
make up for the loss; and
(d) the action taken by Government
in order to check such type of incidents
in future?
Discontinuance of route dispersal
guidelines
561. DR. NARAYAN SINGH
MANAKLAO: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that regional
airlines are being encouraged to improve
connectivity to small cities;
(b) if so, the details of the steps taken/
proposed to be taken in this regard;
(c) whether there is any plan to
discontinue Government's policy of route
dispersal;
(d) if so, the details thereof including
the arrangement to provide connectivity
